text:
The physician may be found liable if they didn't screen for vertebrobasilar insufficiency, for example with a vertebral artery test and a risk-factor review in this 78-year-old, or if they didn't obtain informed consent about the risk of vertebral artery injury before the cervical rotation and extension. The confusion, nausea, and vertigo after treatment point to vertebrobasilar ischemia. The team note is wrong that cervical osteoarthritis is an absolute contraindication to neck treatment, because it is common at this age and usually only calls for gentler, modified technique, so treating him wasn't a breach on that basis alone.

CONFIDENCE: 68
